ec2InstanceFailure.impactDefault: EC2 is not part of the demo architecture.
ec2InstanceFailure.resilienceDefault: No EC2 resilience evaluation was required.
ec2InstanceFailure.impactHigh: A single EC2 instance failure could interrupt application availability.
ec2InstanceFailure.resilienceHigh: Add redundant instances and Auto Scaling to reduce single-instance dependency.
ec2InstanceFailure.impactMedium: Some EC2 capacity may be lost, but additional capacity can continue serving traffic.
ec2InstanceFailure.resilienceMedium: Multiple instances or scaling reduce the effect of one instance failing.

ecsTaskFailure.impactDefault: ECS Fargate is not part of the demo architecture.
ecsTaskFailure.resilienceDefault: No ECS resilience evaluation was required.
ecsTaskFailure.impactHigh: A single ECS task failure could temporarily remove the application workload.
ecsTaskFailure.resilienceHigh: Run multiple tasks and use service-level recovery or scaling.
ecsTaskFailure.impactMedium: One ECS task can fail while other tasks continue serving traffic.
ecsTaskFailure.resilienceMedium: Multiple tasks reduce dependence on a single running task.

rdsFailure.impactDefault: RDS is not part of the demo architecture.
rdsFailure.resilienceDefault: No RDS resilience evaluation was required.
rdsFailure.impactHigh: A database failure could stop application reads and writes until recovery.
rdsFailure.resilienceHigh: Enable Multi-AZ and maintain backups for stronger database resilience.
rdsFailure.resilienceBackupsOnly: Backups support recovery, but they do not provide immediate failover.
rdsFailure.impactMedium: A Multi-AZ database can fail over, although a brief interruption may occur.
rdsFailure.resilienceMedium: Multi-AZ improves availability by providing a standby database.

azOutage.impactDefault: No compute or database services are selected.
azOutage.resilienceDefault: No Availability Zone resilience evaluation was required.
azOutage.impactCritical: An Availability Zone outage could interrupt one or more core application components.
azOutage.resilienceCritical: Spread critical compute and database workloads across multiple Availability Zones.
azOutage.impactMedium: Multi-AZ workloads can continue operating with reduced or shifted capacity.
azOutage.resilienceMedium: Multi-AZ placement reduces dependency on a single Availability Zone.

ec2.management: You manage the operating system and instance configuration.
ec2.bestFor: Workloads that need OS-level control or traditional servers.

ecsFargate.billingModel: Requested container CPU and memory capacity.
ecsFargate.bestFor: Containerized applications without EC2 host management.

rdsPostgres.management: AWS manages infrastructure, patching and backups features.
rdsPostgres.bestFor: Relational data, transactions and SQL workloads.

dynamoDb.bestFor: Predictable low-latency NoSQL access at scale.

alb.bestFor: HTTP/HTTPS applications with multiple backend targets.
alb.keyTradeoff: Balances backends but is not a global content cache.

apiGateway.bestFor: REST/HTTP APIs, especially managed or serverless backends.
apiGateway.keyTradeoff: Rich API features, but it is not a general-purpose load balancer.

cloudfront.bestFor: Static/dynamic content delivery closer to users.
cloudfront.keyTradeoff: Improves delivery latency but does not replace an application backend.

summary.compute: Choose based on how much infrastructure control you need and whether the workload is server-based, containerized, or event-driven.
summary.database: Choose based primarily on data model and access pattern: relational SQL versus scalable NoSQL key/index access.
summary.delivery: These services solve different layers of traffic delivery and are often used together rather than as direct replacements.

multiAz.title: Design for Availability Zone failure

backups.title: Configure and verify backups
backups.description: Define backup retention and confirm restoration procedures.

scaling.title: Plan for scaling

logs.title: Centralize application and infrastructure logs

alarms.title: Create actionable alarms

auditTrail.title: Maintain an audit trail

runbook.title: Document operational runbooks

costReview.title: Review expected cost

recoveryTest.title: Test recovery procedures

ec2.name: Amazon EC2
ec2.description: Virtual servers you manage yourself, for full control over the OS and runtime.

ecsFargate.name: Amazon ECS Fargate
ecsFargate.description: Runs containers without managing servers — AWS handles the underlying infrastructure.

lambda.name: AWS Lambda
lambda.description: Runs code in response to events, with no servers to provision or manage.

rdsPostgres.name: Amazon RDS (PostgreSQL)
rdsPostgres.description: A managed relational database, with AWS handling patching, backups and failover.

dynamoDb.name: Amazon DynamoDB
dynamoDb.description: A managed NoSQL database built for consistent, low-latency access at any scale.

s3.name: Amazon S3
s3.description: Durable object storage for files, backups, static assets and data of any size.

efs.name: Amazon EFS
efs.description: A managed file system that multiple compute instances can mount at once.

vpc.name: Amazon VPC
vpc.description: An isolated network you control, where the rest of your architecture runs.

alb.name: Application Load Balancer
alb.description: Distributes incoming traffic across multiple compute targets for availability.

apiGateway.name: Amazon API Gateway
apiGateway.description: A managed front door for APIs, handling routing, throttling and authorization.

cloudfront.name: Amazon CloudFront
cloudfront.description: A content delivery network that caches content closer to users worldwide.

route53.name: Amazon Route 53
route53.description: A managed DNS service for routing traffic to your application's endpoints.

secretsManager.name: AWS Secrets Manager
secretsManager.description: Stores and rotates credentials so secrets never sit in code or config files.

kms.name: AWS KMS
kms.description: Manages encryption keys used to protect data across your AWS services.

waf.name: AWS WAF
waf.description: A web application firewall that filters malicious traffic before it reaches your app.

cloudwatch.name: Amazon CloudWatch
cloudwatch.description: Collects logs, metrics and alarms for observing how your architecture behaves.

sns.name: Amazon SNS
sns.description: Publishes notifications to many subscribers at once (fan-out messaging).

sqs.name: Amazon SQS
sqs.description: A managed queue that decouples services and smooths out traffic spikes.

eventBridge.name: Amazon EventBridge
eventBridge.description: Routes events between AWS services and applications based on rules.

assessment.title: Assessment Result
assessment.disclaimer: This is an educational portfolio assessment model, not an official AWS Well-Architected Framework review. Each category starts at a baseline of 70 points; specific configuration choices below add or subtract points from there.
assessment.noRulesApplied: No specific factors detected for this category — base score applied.

costEfficiency.duplicateCompute: EC2 and ECS Fargate both selected (possible duplicate compute)
costEfficiency.tooManyFixedInstances: More than 5 fixed EC2 instances with no Auto Scaling

performance.albMultipleTargets: ALB distributing traffic across multiple compute targets

recommendations.title: Recommendations
recommendations.disclaimer: These recommendations are educational, rules-based advice for this demo configuration. They are not an official AWS Well-Architected review and are not a complete security audit.
recommendations.empty: No additional recommendations for this configuration — no matching gaps were detected.

rdsPublic.title: Disable public access on RDS
rdsPublic.explanation: A publicly reachable database can be probed from the internet. Keep RDS private and reach it only from inside the VPC (or a controlled path such as a bastion or VPN).
rdsPublic.concept: RDS public accessibility and network isolation

monitoringAbsent.title: Add CloudWatch for logs, metrics, and alarms
monitoringAbsent.explanation: Without a monitoring service you cannot see failures, latency, or capacity problems until users report them. CloudWatch is the natural operations layer for the services already in this architecture.

singleComputeNoScaling.title: Avoid a single compute instance or task without Auto Scaling
singleComputeNoScaling.explanation: One EC2 instance or one ECS task is a single point of failure, and it cannot absorb load spikes. Run more than one, enable Auto Scaling, or both.

tooManyFixedInstances.title: Turn on Auto Scaling instead of a large fixed EC2 fleet
tooManyFixedInstances.explanation: More than five always-on instances with no scaling usually means you pay for peak capacity all day. Auto Scaling matches capacity to demand.

rdsPrivateSubnet.title: Place RDS in a private subnet
rdsPrivateSubnet.explanation: Databases should not sit on a subnet with a route to the internet. Private subnet placement is the usual production pattern in a VPC.

rdsEncryption.title: Enable encryption at rest for RDS
rdsEncryption.explanation: Unencrypted storage exposes data if a snapshot or volume is copied out of the account. Encryption at rest is a baseline RDS control.

s3PublicBlocked.title: Block public access on S3
s3PublicBlocked.explanation: Objects become internet-readable if the bucket (or an object ACL) allows public access. Block Public Access is the default-safe control for most buckets.

rdsBackups.title: Enable automated RDS backups
rdsBackups.explanation: Without backups, a failed migration or accidental delete has no restore path. Automated backups also underpin point-in-time recovery.
rdsBackups.concept: RDS automated backups and point-in-time recovery

rdsMultiAz.title: Enable Multi-AZ for RDS
rdsMultiAz.explanation: A single-AZ database is unavailable if that Availability Zone fails. Multi-AZ keeps a standby in another AZ and fails over automatically.

s3Encryption.title: Enable encryption for S3 objects
s3Encryption.explanation: Encryption at rest protects object data in the bucket and in snapshots of that data. Use bucket default encryption so new objects inherit it.

s3Versioning.title: Enable S3 versioning
s3Versioning.explanation: Versioning keeps prior object versions so an overwrite or delete can be undone. It is a basic durability control for important buckets.

ec2MultiAz.title: Spread EC2 across multiple Availability Zones
ec2MultiAz.explanation: Instances in one AZ share that AZ's failure domain. Multi-AZ placement keeps the application running if one data center is lost.

ecsMultiAz.title: Spread ECS Fargate tasks across multiple Availability Zones
ecsMultiAz.explanation: Tasks in a single AZ go down together if that AZ fails. Multi-AZ task placement is the usual reliability setting for Fargate services.

cloudfrontHttps.title: Require HTTPS on CloudFront
cloudfrontHttps.explanation: HTTP at the CDN edge sends cookies and tokens in the clear. Redirect viewers to HTTPS before they reach the origin.

albHttps.title: Require HTTPS on the Application Load Balancer
albHttps.explanation: An HTTP-only ALB listener exposes traffic on the path into the VPC. Terminate TLS on the load balancer (or redirect HTTP to HTTPS).

cloudwatchLogs.title: Enable CloudWatch logs
cloudwatchLogs.explanation: Metrics show that something is wrong; logs show why. Turn on log collection for the compute and application layers you already selected.

cloudwatchAlarms.title: Enable CloudWatch alarms
cloudwatchAlarms.explanation: Logs and metrics without alarms still require someone to watch dashboards. Alarms notify you when error rate, latency, or capacity crosses a threshold.

secretsManagerEnabled.title: Use Secrets Manager for credentials instead of leaving it unused
secretsManagerEnabled.explanation: The service is selected but secrets management is off, so credentials can still end up in code or config. Enable rotation and retrieval through Secrets Manager.

duplicateCompute.title: Review running both EC2 and ECS Fargate
duplicateCompute.explanation: Two general-purpose compute platforms often means duplicated patching, networking, and cost. Keep both only when there is a deliberate split (for example, a legacy VM plus new containers).

cloudfrontRestrictedOrigin.title: Restrict CloudFront origin access
cloudfrontRestrictedOrigin.explanation: If viewers can bypass CloudFront and hit the origin directly, edge controls (HTTPS, WAF, caching) are optional. Restrict the origin so traffic must come through the distribution.

ec2PrivatePlacement.title: Place EC2 instances in a private subnet
ec2PrivatePlacement.explanation: Public-subnet instances have a path to the internet and a larger attack surface. Put application servers in private subnets and expose them through a load balancer.

wafForPublicEntry.title: Consider AWS WAF in front of the public HTTP entry
wafForPublicEntry.explanation: This architecture already has ALB or CloudFront facing the network. WAF can filter common web exploits before they reach the origin. It is optional, not a substitute for HTTPS and private databases.
wafForPublicEntry.concept: AWS WAF on CloudFront or ALB

secretsManagerForRds.title: Consider Secrets Manager for RDS credentials
secretsManagerForRds.explanation: A database is in the architecture, so something must store the password. Secrets Manager keeps credentials out of images and environment files and can rotate them.

albForMultipleTargets.title: Consider an Application Load Balancer for multiple compute targets
albForMultipleTargets.explanation: More than one EC2 instance or ECS task needs a way to share traffic and to survive a single target failing. An ALB is the usual HTTP front door for that pattern.
